blocks.c: I want to tell you I hesitated. I hesitated for less time than it takes to describe, and then I stepped out, because the alternative was riding back up not knowing, and I have never in my life been able to do that.
The air was fine. Room temperature. Slight smell of floor polish.
I walked to the security desk. There was a visitor log on it: the old paper kind, a spiral book with columns for NAME, VISITING, IN, OUT.
Hundreds of names, going back pages, in dozens of different hands, and every single one had a time in the IN column.
Not one of them had a time in the OUT column.
I found my own name on the fourth page from the front.
My handwriting. My actual handwriting, the stupid loop I put on the R, and I had not touched that book, and I had been out of the elevator for ninety seconds.
I did the thing you would do. I took out my pen, and I wrote a time in the OUT column beside my name, and it was 01:22, and I pressed hard.
The lights went out on the whole floor.
Every light. Instantly. And in the black, from over by the elevators, a voice that was not loud and was not close said, very clearly, with what I swear was interest:
